messages:
incident-bot: ALERT P1 — gpu-queue-length high in eu-west-1
> metric: gpu_pool.queue_length(gpu-pool-3) = 12,600 (5m avg) | threshold=2,000 | growth=+8x in 10m
> symptoms: latency spike -> 95th token latency 2.1s, increased 429 throttles
> paging: oncall

Elena SRE: I’m oncall. joining bridge now. pinging infra + ml.

Amir (ML): I see a big spike in jobs with long sequence-lengths from a single customer key. Looks like batched rerank and some big-context chat runs.

Matt (infra): infra logs show autoscaler repeatedly requested new GPUs but cloud reported "quota_exceeded" and then rate-limited scale-up calls. also some kube pods Pending with "InsufficientNVIDIAComGPU".

Sara Ops: Support is getting customer pings. Major customers in EU are seeing 429s. Support-June on standby to triage inbound.

Support-June: We have three customers reporting timeouts and 429s. Ticket ids: #2322, #2330, #2337. Let me know when we have mitigation notes to share.

Elena SRE: Quick plan: 1) open bridge, 2) try immediate mitigations (soft-throttle heavy keys, route non-critical traffic to cpu models), 3) provider quota support request, 4) longer term postmortem.

oncall-bridge-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/b/incident-1776543210

Matt (infra): Adding details — autoscaler logs (excerpt):
```
2026-03-15T09:11:02Z scale-request: want=24 current=10
2026-03-15T09:11:03Z provider: quota_exceeded GPUs request=14 available=0
2026-03-15T09:11:05Z scale-retry backoff=30s
2026-03-15T09:11:30Z scale-request: want=24 current=10
2026-03-15T09:11:31Z provider: rate_limit 429
```
also provider shows recent capacity churn in eu-west-1

Amir (ML): Can we short-circuit the biggest batchers by applying per-api-key concurrency limits at the gateway? That would relieve the queue immediately for everyone else.

Elena SRE: Yes. Matt, can we flip emergency token-bucket throttle for top N keys? Sara, coordinate messaging.

Matt (infra): On it — adding a transient quota for heavy keys. Command:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/quotas -d '{"key":"tenant:big-ram","max_inflight":4}'
```
Applied to two keys that accounted for ~60% of queued work. watch queue.

infra-bot: Quota update: tenant:big-ram max_inflight=4 (applied by matt)

Elena SRE: Also enabling fallback routing for non-SLA routes -> cpu-optimized models to reduce GPU contention. Amir, is quality drop acceptable for these customers short-term?

Amir (ML): For low-tier traffic yes. I'll publish a fallback model version and tag it for route: non-sla-eu.

Matt (infra): Fallback routing switch done.

Elena SRE: Observed immediate queue decrease from 12.6k -> 4.2k in 3 minutes. Token latency improved but still above SLO.

Support-June: Notifying affected customers: "We’ve applied emergency throttles and fallback routing; you may see degraded performance for some requests while we restore full capacity." Sending to the three impacted accounts now.

Product CTO: Heads-up: large customer X flagged SLA impact. Keep me posted on ETA to full restore.

Matt (infra): Provider support responded — they have a multi-hour backlog for GPU quota increase. They recommended spinning up from another region or launching rented capacity from partner. Partner rack available in eu-central with 40 GPUs but requires manual provisioning.

Elena SRE: Can we failover traffic to eu-central temporarily? What about latency and data residency? Need decision.

Matt (infra): We can route a small percent (10-20%) to eu-central for non-EU-customer-sensitive data. That will reduce pressure. Initiating canary roll now.

infra-bot: Route update: +15% traffic -> eu-central-coldpool (applied by matt)

Elena SRE: Good. Queue now 4.2k -> 2.1k after throttles + fallback + partial failover. Still monitoring.

Amir (ML): Side note: several long-context jobs used KV caching but with huge sequences; recommend temporarily rejecting sequences > 16k tokens for non-critical lanes.

Matt (infra): Blocking rule applied at gateway: reject seq_len>16000 for route non-sla-eu.

Elena SRE: Bridge update: we have stabilization. Immediate mitigation sequence completed. Next: recovery steps and customer comms. Marking incident as "mitigated" for paging.

incident-bot: Incident status update: P1 -> mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:32:00Z (approx). Monitoring continues.

Support-June: I'll follow up with each impacted customer with timeline and remediation summary.

Elena SRE: Post-incident notes (quick):
- Root cause: autoscaler requests were blocked by provider GPU quota exhaustion + provider-side rate limiting; combined with a concentrated spike from one tenant (batch rerank) -> queue growth and throttles.
- Immediate mitigations: per-tenant concurrency caps, fallback routing to CPU models, partial regional failover, gateway blocking for extreme sequence lengths, manual partner capacity bring-up.
- Customer impact: several enterprise customers saw elevated 429s and latency for ~20-45 minutes depending on region; no data loss.

Elena SRE: Action items (assignments inline):
1) Update autoscaler retry/backoff and surface provider quota errors more clearly in alerts — owner: Matt (infra).
2) Add automated per-key throttling capability to Runbook for emergency — owner: Sara Ops + Matt — due 2 weeks.
3) Simulate concentrated-tenant surge in chaos tests (include large sequence lengths) — owner: Amir (ML) + Eng QE — due 3 weeks.
4) Add reserve pool / partner warm-standby for eu-west-1 to avoid single-provider exhaust — owner: Product CTO + Matt — due 1 month.
5) Improve alert thresholds: alert earlier on rate limit counts and scale-request failures — owner: Elena SRE — due 1 week.

Product CTO: Agree on priority for reserve pool; will scope procurement with infra.

Matt (infra): Will open PRs for clearer autoscaler metrics + alerting. Also file support ticket with provider for quota increase and request SLA improvement.

Amir (ML): Will add template fallback models and a small config to automatically route lower-priority keys to them under pressure.

Sara Ops: I'll draft customer-facing post-incident summary for legal/comms review.

Elena SRE: Final: we’ll keep monitoring for 2 hours for regression. If queue stabilizes under 2k and 95th token latency <1s for 30m, we close the incident. Thanks team.

incident-bot: Monitoring window started. next automated check in 15m."
